SAP LABS Interview Experience 
 
SAP Labs India is SAP's largest Research and Development centre outside its headquarters in 
Germany. It has one of the best and most used ERP software and cloud computing service in the 
world. 
Eligibility criteria: 70 % or 7 CGPA and above in current graduating degree and 60% in 10th & 12th 
Job description: Any (Developer/QA/Support/DevOps/Dev Support) 
Job location: Bangalore/Pune/Mumbai/Gurgaon 
 
Coding test  
 
The test was held on 4 August, total duration 45 minutes and comprised of two very simple questions. 
It was SHL Proctored and had support for all the major languages with IDE. The questions were :   
1. There are two servers in a firm each server gets alternate request given an array of requests 
print the sum of requests handled by server1 
Example.  
   Requests= {2,3,6,8,9,7} 
   Server1 will get requests 2,6,9 so sum= 2+6+9 = 17  
   So expected output was 17 
 
2. Second question was to find out prime numbers in a given range which was again a very easy 
question so I almost finished the test in 15-20 minutes. 
The results were declared on 8 August and 40 students were shortlisted. 
 
Technical Interview I (9 August 9:30 am) 
 
It was conducted on Microsoft Teams Platform. It lasted for around 45-50 min. 
The interviewer asked me whether we are given holidays for training or am I at college but as it was 
Moharram we were having holiday so I told him that, then he said after getting internship you won’t 
get any such holidays and will have to work even on holidays so will you like it. I answered him saying 
it will be fun to learn new things even on holidays. (Not really but what else could I have answered). 
Then he asked me to start with my introduction and asked me to choose any of the technical skill I 
mentioned in my resume. I choose C++ then he asked me about static class, I was not able to answer 
properly, so he changed his question and asked tell me about the types of classes you know in C++, I 
explained him in brief about Abstract class, Friend class, Base class and derived class.

Then I was asked what is object-oriented programming, what is the difference between abstraction 
and encapsulation. To explain the four pillars of OOPS using examples I answered all questions 
correctly and explained the four concepts with real life examples so the interviewer was impressed 
and said I liked the way you relate things to life. 
Later on, I was asked Architectural design of how would I store the Information of VJTI in database 
and also in C++ so I talked about the tables I would create in DBMS and about the classes in C++ and 
inherit them and so on. 
 Then he asked me to pick any of the project I mentioned in my resume and explain it to him, I 
explained my project and my contribution Then I was asked where would my project fail, I told where 
it previously failed, how we handled it and in what cases it may fail in future.  
I was asked which sorting algorithms do I know, I talked about merge sort, quick sort, Insertion sort 
and Bubble sort, then I was asked which is the quickest and the most time taking sorting algorithm 
and which consumes most space, I answered the questions mentioning the time and space 
complexity of four of them. 
Finally, he said he has no questions further and I can ask question if I have any. I asked him about the 
work culture at SAP  
After 5 mins I received a dm that am selected for the second technical round. 
 
Technical Interview II (9 August 2:30 pm) 
 
The Interviewer started with his introduction then I introduced myself. Then he asked me to find the 
time complexity of the code in chatbox. 
The question was  
 
For( int i=0;i<n;i++) 
   For(int j=0;j<n;j+=i) 
{ 
Code taking O(1) space 
} 
After seeing two for loops, I quickly answered O(n2) without looking carefully at the question. Then 
the interviewer told me to look at the question carefully and then I saw it and explained it to 
interviewer how the time complexity would be O(nlogn) 
 
Then the second question given again in the chat box and if was to delete a node from linked list given 
the address of that node and not the head node, I previously solved this question(Delete Node in a 
Linked List - LeetCode) so I answered it correctly.

The next question was given a string print the frequency of the letters in the string. 
For example : 
Input: Aishwarya 
Output: A  1 
a  2 
h  1 
i  1 
r  1 
s  1 
w  1 
y  1 
 I was asked to share the screen and solve the question locally on any code editor. I solved the 
question using HashMap to calculate the frequency and using a set to find out the alphabets in string. 
The interviewer asked me whether I can take a complete line as input so I told him since I have not 
used the getline function we cannot input complete line. 
As the next question I got an image of various tables in a society’s database, I was given some time to 
understand the schema of tables and hence the complete database. Then I was asked how would I 
write a query to find out the members in a particular building having more than one flat. The 
Database had various tables and various wings, buildings and a complex connectivity among them, so 
I don’t remember what I answered exactly but the Interviewer was satisfied with my answer. 
The next question was to find the probability of two ants colliding if three ants were standing on the 
vertices of the triangle and can move only along the edges. I was not able to answer the question 
exactly but I explained the interviewer the logic and as we were short of time so he also told me to 
find the answer later on and he’s done with asking questions I can ask him question.  I asked him what 
tech stacks I should learn in order to contribute better towards SAP if I get selected? To which he 
answered that it completely depends on that time’s requirement and cannot be told before hand He 
also told me about SAP culture and how they judge interns before giving them pre placement offer. 
 
HR interview (9 August around 6:30pm) 
 
The HR was very friendly, she asked me to introduce myself, about my interest and the role I would 
prefer. She listened to my introduction patiently and then told me that she’s done with her questions 
and I can ask her any question if I wish to. I asked her that If I get selected as a Inter what will be the 
exact work location? She told me that it depends on that time’s requirement wherever Interns are 
required, we would be appointed at that location and we should be flexible with any of the given 
location.

Tips: 
 
 
Prepare a short introduction so that you do not miss out anything during the interview, The 
intro should be short but explanatory and must cover all important aspects (Almost every 
interviewer asks to give one)  
 
While answering be confident, explain your thought process and keep continuously 
interacting. Even if you don’t remember anything speak it out (it’s okay, no one can be 
perfect and remember everything), the interviewer will either ask you something similar or 
give you some hint 
 
Do not lie on your resume, interviewers ask a lot of questions based on it. 
 
Have a clear Understanding of questions and rather than assuming, it is always better to ask 
the interviewers to repeat/explain the question again. 
 
In coding questions/puzzles the interviewer wants to check your approach to solve the 
problem so don’t worry too much if you forget the syntax or formulas. 
 
If you don’t know or are not sure about something, say so rather than wasting time or making 
random guesses; the interviewers usually help or give hints to you. (No one expects you to 
know everything) 
 
Research about the company and keep at least 2-3 good questions ready, so when the 
interviewer asks if you have any questions for them you are prepared. Also asking a question 
has an advantage that most of times you get a clear idea you will be selected for the next 
round or not. 
 
 
 
 
ALL THE BEST!!!
